newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Phillips sees 25,000 bpd from Venezuelan oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Phillips sees 25,000 bpd from Venezuelan oilfield.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum plans to hike output from Venezuela's Ambrosio oilfield to at least 25,000 barrels per day (bpd) within 3-6 years, a company official said Wednesday.
Phillips won a contract to operate the field, located offshore in Lake Maracaibo, with a cash bid of $31 million in Venezuela's third oil contract round.
+We see good potential in this fractured cretacious reservoir. We plan to develop it with horizontal drilling and stimulation,+ said Phillips global ventures manager Paul Appel.

Oil output has fallen sharply to 1,500 bpd, but Appel said the field probably contained over 100 million barrels of medium density crude in a difficult geological formation. The company planned to invest $200 million over the 20 year life of the contract.
Only two companies bid for the field, with Enron Oil and Gas losing the contract by $15 million.
Ambrosio also had significant natural gas potential, with 870 billion cubic feet of gas in place and current production of 13 million cubic feet per day.
Appel said the company had no concrete plans for expanding gas production, although a market for it existed in western Venezuela.
